definitions.definition: Processes undertaken by an APRA-regulated entity or its service provider which, if disrupted beyond tolerance levels, would have a material adverse impact on its depositors, policyholders, beneficiaries or other customers, or its role in the financial system.

all_entities: Systems and IT infrastructure needed to support critical operations

definitions.definition: The maximum acceptable level of disruption an APRA-regulated entity is willing to accept for a critical operation. Must be set for: (1) Maximum period of time tolerable for disruption (downtime); (2) Maximum extent of data loss accepted; and (3) Minimum service levels maintained while operating under alternative arrangements.

A service provider on which an APRA-regulated entity relies to undertake a critical operation or that exposes it to material operational risk. Can be a third party, related party, or connected entity.

A party that a service provider relies upon in delivering services to an APRA-regulated entity (i.e. subcontractor of a material service provider). Entities must manage risks of fourth parties supporting critical operations.
Information and information technology, including software, hardware and data (both soft and hard copy).
An actual or potential compromise of information security (confidentiality, integrity, or availability).
The totality of resources, skills and controls which provide the ability and capacity to maintain information security.
Criticality refers to the potential impact of a loss of availability. Sensitivity refers to the potential impact of a loss of confidentiality or integrity.

A material arrangement where the service provided is undertaken outside Australia. Includes arrangements where the service provider is incorporated in Australia, but the physical location of the service/data is offshore. Requires prior notification to APRA.
